questions.q: Which two fields of a floating-point number control its range and its precision, respectively?
options: Sign and mantissa
Exponent and sign
Exponent and mantissa
Mantissa and sign
questions.explain: The exponent sets how large or small a value can get (range); the mantissa sets how many significant digits are kept (precision). The sign bit only controls positive vs. negative.

questions.q: A tensor holding the value 70,000.0 is cast to torch.float16. What happens?
options: It rounds to 70,000 with slightly less precision
It overflows to inf, because FP16's largest finite value is 65,504
PyTorch raises a RuntimeError
It is silently promoted back to float32
questions.explain: FP16's 5-bit exponent limits its largest representable finite value to 65,504. A value above that overflows to infinity rather than raising an error.

questions.q: Why can BF16 represent the same value that overflows in FP16?
options: BF16 uses more total bits than FP16
BF16 has a larger mantissa than FP16
BF16 keeps the same 8-bit exponent as FP32, giving it FP32's dynamic range
BF16 is not a real IEEE-style floating-point format
questions.explain: BF16 is also 16 bits total, but it allocates 8 bits to the exponent (same as FP32) and only 7 to the mantissa, trading precision for FP32's much larger range.

questions.q: Compared to FP32, what does converting a tensor to FP16 or BF16 primarily cost you?
options: Nothing — both are strictly more accurate than FP32
Precision (fewer significant digits), in exchange for less memory and faster compute on supporting hardware
The ability to use the tensor in a forward pass at all
Compatibility with torch.tensor()
questions.explain: Both 16-bit formats use fewer mantissa bits than FP32, so they keep fewer significant digits. The payoff is half the memory footprint and faster matrix multiplies on GPUs with 16-bit tensor cores.

questions.q: What does torch.finfo(torch.bfloat16) let you inspect?
options: The number of CUDA cores available for bfloat16 operations
The min, max, and resolution (precision) limits of the bfloat16 dtype
Whether the current GPU supports bfloat16
The memory address of a bfloat16 tensor
questions.explain: torch.finfo() reports the numeric limits of a floating-point dtype — its smallest and largest representable values and its precision (resolution) — not hardware availability.
